statement: For the special case of Reed–Solomon codes, Theorem 5 states that any polynomial √ generator has MCA for γ close to the code’s list-decoding bound 1 − ρ. In probabilistic proofs, distance preservation at a larger distance typically implies more efficient verification. √ Can one bound the MCA error for distances γ beyond 1 − ρ? [5] conjectures MCA for the univariate powers generator for γ close to the code’s capacity 1 − ρ, and similar conjectures on Reed–Solomon codes are sometimes used in practice for efficiency. Yet [25, 23] shows that this is too much to hope for: there is a family of Reed–Solomon codes for which distance preservation fails for the affine line generator x 7→ (1, x) when γ is close to the code’s capacity 1 − ρ. Understanding whether MCA holds between the list-decoding and capacity bounds remains open.
